title: The Grothendieck construction between the telescope monad and contextads
summary: A telescope is a list of stages in which each stage is a family indexed over the Grothendieck construction of the previous ones. The telescope monad stacks stages as the free-monoid 2-monad on spans, whereas a contextad collapses two stages into one by a dependent sum. This paper derives both from the span of single stages, and thereby explains why the strict algebras of the telescope monad are contextads. The link is the Grothendieck extension of a span.
